newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Murdoch readies his son for the big time.
newsitem.headline: Murdoch readies his son for the big time.

text.p: By all accounts, Lachlan Murdoch has had lot of fun during his three years in Australia as an apprentice in a small part of News Corp's global empire.
But his father, News Corp founder and executive chairman Rupert Murdoch on Tuesday put his elder son on notice that the training is over -- it is time to take charge.

Lachlan, his 66-year-old father said in a statement from Los Angeles, would now head the Australian offshoot News Ltd which encompasses newspapers, pay television, sports management, and the half share in a loss-making airline.
A difficult task at the best of times and made harder when you are only 25 years old. Even if you are a Princeton graduate.
One analyst, confident that Lachlan would prove the cynics wrong, noted that he was older than his father was when he took control of his first newspaper, the Adelaide News.
"How old was his dad when he took over? Twenty-one. That is the question that everyone is going to be asking."
Either way, Lachlan was not likely to make any key decisions without reference to a higher authority.

"Lachlan is running it but I am sure he is looking over his shoulder getting some advice," said one analyst who, like most, are reluctant to go public with their comments about the company at any time.
The significance of the latest statement, analysts said, was that it provides the strongest sign yet that Lachlan rather than his elder sister Elisabeth was being annointed by their father.
Elisabeth, 28, is an executive with the News Corp affiliate BSkyB in London.
The guessing game about succession will remain just that, however, until Rupert Murdoch decides to stand aside and he has given no sign that this will happen anytime soon.
Lachlan, with boyish good looks and an easy charm which has impressed his journalistic colleagues in Sydney and Brisbane, has mimicked his father's early post-graduate experience.
Like his father he has worked in newsrooms, rolled up his shirt sleeves in printing rooms, and taken charge of large operations at a young age.
Born in London, he became a U.S. citizen in 1993 and graduated from the Ivy League university of Princeton the following year with an arts degree majoring in philosophy.

He was appointed general manager of the Queensland Newspapers group in 1994 and was made managing director of News Ltd in September last year. Signficantly in the succession stakes, Lachlan was appointed to the board of parent company News Corp one month later.
"You would have to say Lachlan is the favoured one at this time," said another local analyst. "He is the only one on the board (of News Corp)."
It has not been all hard work for Lachlan during his stay in Australia, especially if the gossip magazines and columnists are to be believed.

A birthday party he held in Sydney last May for a girlfriend became a scramble among socialities for invitations while he has also been seen dining with fellow mini-magnate James Packer, the son of billionaire Kerry Packer.

The two were rivals in the development of the Super League rugby league competition, which shows on the Foxtel pay-television service part-owned by News. James worked the phones on behalf of the establishment Australian Rugby League which airs on his father's Nine Network.
While James is a few years old than Lachlan, neither can escape the scrutiny of those who think that they are only nominally in charge.
"Who do you think is really running it (News Ltd)? It is the same thing with James Packer," said one analyst.
"I would be flabbergasted if either of them were in a position to make a decision off their own bat without having to get it through appropriate people."
